subject: Agriculture
title: Crop Rotation Basics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Crop Rotation Basics.

hook.text: Planting the same crop on the same field every year exhausts the soil. Medieval farmers had a fix.

buildup.text: The two-field system alternated: grow wheat one year, leave the field fallow the next to recover.

discovery.text: The three-field system was better—wheat, then oats or barley, then fallow. One-third rested instead of half.

twist.text: This seemingly small change boosted output by 50%. More food meant more people, more villages, more trade.

climax.text: Three-field rotation spread across Europe by 1000 CE and powered the population boom of the High Middle Ages.

punchline.text: A third field changed the math—and fed a continent.

quiz.question: How did the three-field system improve on the two-field system?
options: Only one-third of land rested instead of half, boosting yields by 50%
